newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Goodyear returns to S. Africa with $121 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear returns to S. Africa with $121 million deal.

text.p: Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co. said Monday it was returning to South Africa after pulling out in 1989, by buying 60 percent of local tire maker Contred (Pty) Ltd. for $121 million, including assumed debt.
The U.S. tire giant will buy the stake from Anglovaal Industries Ltd. (AVI), which in turn will purchase the entire share capital of Contred from its Consol Ltd. unit.

Tycon, the tire-making part of Contred, was acquired by Consol from Goodyear when Goodyear disinvested from South Africa in 1989. Tycon manufactures, markets and distributes tyres under the Goodyear and Kelly brand names and manufactures and markets engineered products.
Contred also owns Tredcor which distributes tires through 195 retail outlets and retreads tires, and Arctic which markets pre-cured tread rubber.
Contred, based in Uitenhage near Port Elizabeth, reported net attributable earnings of 108.3 million rand ($23.2 million) on revenues of 1.82 billion rand ($390.6 million) in the year ended June 30.
Goodyear Chairman Samir Gibara said the Uitenhage plant would be integrated into Goodyear's global network, enabling it to become an export source for Goodyear.
"Furthermore, Contred provides Goodyear with a powerful platform from which to seek opportunities in the African content," he said in a statement.
Richard Savage, managing director of AVI which will retain 40 percent of Contred, said the link with Goodyear would strengthen Contred's position in a tough market.

"The reduction of import tariffs in South Africa and the opening up of the South African economy means that competitive pressures have intensified. In order to become globally competitive, many South African manufacturers are forging closer international links," he said.

Savage added that the deal would leave Consol, in which AVI has a majority stake, as a focused packaging group with sufficient funds to pay down debt and develop its packaging interests, notably in southern Africa.
Goodyear's stock fell 12.5 cents to $49.375 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
